previous.indication: Melanoma at high risk of recurrence after surgery
previous.summary: Moderna and Merck reported Phase 3 results for a vaccine made individually for each patient's tumour and given with the immunotherapy pembrolizumab. The risk of the melanoma returning or of death was 42% lower than with pembrolizumab alone. The vaccine is not yet approved.
previous.headline: A personalised mRNA vaccine given with pembrolizumab was reported to cut the risk of melanoma returning or causing death by 42% in a Phase 3 trial

corrected.indication: Completely resected stage IIB–IV cutaneous melanoma
corrected.summary: In October 2026, Moderna and Merck reported results from INTerpath-001, comparing intismeran autogene plus pembrolizumab with pembrolizumab alone after complete resection of stage IIB–IV cutaneous melanoma. The combination reduced the reported risk of recurrence or death by 42%. This finding concerns the combined postoperative regimen, not intismeran alone or treatment of unresectable melanoma.

trial_decisions.reason: Keep tentative: Part D explicitly gives mRNA-4157 plus pembrolizumab to participants with completely resected stage II/III/IV cutaneous melanoma. Other arms do not establish this association. No promotion or score change.
Retain KEYNOTE-942: an adjuvant cohort receives mRNA-4157 plus pembrolizumab following complete resection.
Retain INTerpath-001: the named origin study explicitly compares the complete combination after resection of stage IIB–IV cutaneous melanoma.
Reject INTerpath-012: it requires unresectable stage III/IV melanoma and measurable disease, incompatible with the postoperative disease-free claim.
